Use case: stylized-concept. Create a production PNG sprite atlas with REAL TRANSPARENT background for a top-down pixel art dungeon game. Reference image is style and material reference ONLY: use the LOW walls in its LEFT room, not the tall bottom wall samples. Theme: rounded low gray granite with sparse green moss.
Exactly FOUR isolated sprites arranged in a spacious equal 2x2 grid with centers at 25%/75% canvas coordinates. Top left: ONE low wall cell, broad almost square stone top, small short front face, waist-high. Top right: ONE low wall cell of same footprint and height with alternate cracks. These are compact single-cell wall blocks, NOT a long wall, NOT a room, NOT a corner, NOT an isometric diamond. Straight horizontal front edge, overhead RPG view, see broad upper surface occupying at least two-thirds height and short vertical face below. Almost square overall silhouette, nearly fill each quadrant with generous transparent margin for cropping. Bottom left: small mossy rock cluster. Bottom right: broken short stone marker. Props low and broad, under one adventurer's height.
Match crisp chunky pixel shading of reference, readable at 64px. Consistent lighting upper left, no blur. All four sprites completely separate with no touching. No labels, text, frame, floor, character, cast shadow outside sprite, backdrop or painted checkerboard. Fully opaque painted objects, alpha=0 elsewhere. Transparent background.
